analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md, head lines 595-611: a new paragraph describing the Gated DeltaNet prefill recurrence kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. For prompt windows of at least 16 unmasked positions, the first window per kernel instantiation in a process probes the `packed` kernel and then the `rows` kernel against `gated_delta_step` on a fixed probe window. It keeps the first one that matches bit for bit, else the stock kernel. Decode, MTP verification, masked updates and short windows stay on the stock kernel. `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED` is an A/B override.

The patch changes no code, key handling, wire format or trust-boundary behavior, so I found no regression. Relevant threat IDs are T-041 and T-007. Nothing in the text widens the prefix-cache at-rest surface, TTL, HMAC naming, salt scoping or authentication. The claim that a bit-exact kernel leaves recurrent state unchanged for checkpoint capture is a correctness assertion in prose. I could not verify it because the underlying GatedDelta.swift change is not in the supplied evidence. If the code PR alters kernel selection, a later pass should check two things. First, that the bit-exactness probe cannot be bypassed by the env override in a production deployment. Second, that checkpoints captured under one kernel stay valid when restored under another, as T-041 SSD checkpoint integrity assumes. The rest of the supplied file text is unchanged surrounding documentation and I flagged nothing in it. No threat-model update appears necessary for this doc-only change.
